prompts.prompt: Review the change in changes.diff before it merges (the new file is also at src/wallet.js; src/db.js is existing code it uses). This handler moves real money, so be thorough. Write review.md with each finding's severity (CRITICAL, IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION), file:line, the problem, and a concrete fix, ordered by severity. Do not modify any code. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's checklist makes atomicity (read-modify-write without conditions) and missing error handling on external calls CRITICAL, and expects reuse of existing helpers. A strong answer ranks the unconditional db.put race and the unchecked fetch at the top and points at the existing db.putIf; a generic review often rates the fetch issue as a nit and suggests a new locking scheme instead of the helper already in db.js.

floor_checks.text: review.md cites the balance read-modify-write lines in wallet.js

rubric.pass: Rated CRITICAL; explains that concurrent withdrawals both read the old balance and one debit is lost
rubric.partial: Found but rated below CRITICAL, or impact not explained

rubric.criterion: Fix for the race uses what the codebase already has
rubric.pass: Recommends db.putIf(walletId, wallet, oldBalance) with retry on ConditionalCheckFailed (or an equivalent conditional update), not a new lock
rubric.partial: Recommends a conditional write but ignores putIf or proposes an in-process mutex alongside it
rubric.fail: Recommends an in-memory lock/mutex only, or no fix

rubric.criterion: External rate call and input handling
rubric.pass: Flags fetch with no res.ok/timeout/try-catch (rated high, per the skill's CRITICAL bucket) and unvalidated amount (negative credits the wallet) or unencoded currency in the URL
rubric.partial: Flags one of these two groups

rubric.criterion: Review format the skill asks for
rubric.pass: Every finding has severity, file:line, problem, fix; ordered CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION; also catches the DEBUG console.log of the request body and missing null check on wallet
rubric.partial: Format followed but one of the secondary findings missing or misordered
rubric.fail: Unordered prose, no line references, or no fixes

rubric.pass: Every finding is real in the diff; no claims about SQL injection, auth, or code not shown
rubric.partial: One speculative finding clearly labeled as such

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Are the two money-losing bugs at the top?

prompts.prompt: Write the pull request description for this branch into pr-body.md, using notes.md (my scratch notes from the branch) and changes.diff as the source. A reviewer who has not seen the branch will read it. Do not create the PR. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill requires PR text that describes the final state only: no 'previously', no 'found during review round 2', no 'updated per feedback', no em dashes, plus what/why/how to test. notes.md is full of history narration; without the skill, models usually carry some of it forward.

floor_checks.check: test -f pr-body.md && ! grep -qiE 'previously|found during|review round|round [0-9]|per feedback|updated per|was fixed|fixed it|renamed' pr-body.md
test -f pr-body.md && python3 -c "import sys;t=open('pr-body.md',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(1 if (chr(8212) in t or chr(8211) in t) else 0)"

rubric.pass: States the two endpoints and FX conversion, why (non-USD wallets), and how to test with npm test and the curl from notes.md
rubric.fail: Missing how to test, or only a title

rubric.pass: No trace of history: no USD-only past, no double-call fix, no Priya rename, no 'now'
rubric.partial: One residual 'now supports' or similar contrast

rubric.criterion: Reads like a person wrote it
rubric.pass: Short, plain, no promotional words or filler, no padded bullet lists
rubric.partial: Mostly plain with one or two AI tells
rubric.fail: Boilerplate sections, buzzwords, or long generated prose

prompts.prompt: We have no network access here, so do not run gh or git against a remote. Write commands.sh with the exact commands you would run, with a comment line above each step, to: (1) open the PR for this branch against main using pr-body.md as the body; (2) get someone else's PR #57 in acme/wallet onto disk so you can read every changed file (this directory is my main checkout and has uncommitted work); (3) post review findings from review.md on #57 so I can check them before anyone else sees them, and submit them later; (4) reply to the two open review comments on my PR #41. Do not execute anything. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill prescribes draft PRs, checking the current checkout and git worktree list before creating a separate absolute-path checkout (never gh pr checkout in the primary checkout), a pending review created through the reviews API with the id captured and submission as a separate authorized step, and one user confirmation per comment reply. A generic answer typically runs gh pr checkout in place, uses gh pr review (which submits immediately), and batches replies.

floor_checks.text: Does not use gh pr review, which submits immediately
floor_checks.check: test -f commands.sh && ! grep -qE '^\s*gh pr review' commands.sh

rubric.pass: gh pr create --draft --base main --body-file pr-body.md (or equivalent)
rubric.partial: Draft but body passed inline in a way that breaks on quotes

rubric.pass: Checks git branch/worktree list first, then git worktree add (or a clone under pr-reviews/57) at an absolute path and runs gh pr checkout only inside it
rubric.partial: Uses a separate directory but a relative path or skips the existing-checkout check
rubric.fail: gh pr checkout 57 in the current main checkout with uncommitted work

rubric.fail: Replies posted with no confirmation gate, or step missing
